Question: What physical and orbital characteristics (such as absolute magnitude, estimated diameter, and velocity) are the strongest indicators of whether a near-Earth asteroid is classified as potentially hazardous?

Variables that might be related:
- Miss distance
- Size (diameter)
- Velocity

https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sunethjayawardana/nasa-near-earth-objects-neo-full-dataset

• Near-Earth Objects (NEOs): Any asteroid or comet that comes within 1.3 AU of the Sun.
• Potentially Hazardous Asteroids (PHAs): A specific subset of NEOs that pose a more significant threat. To be classified as a PHA, the asteroid must:
	- Come within 0.05 AU of Earth (about 4.6 million miles or 7.5 million kilometers).
	- Be large enough to cause significant regional damage (typically larger than 140 meters or 460 feet in diameter).

Brook's Workspace:
```{r}
#Basic consideration, what percent of asteroids are hazardous -
neo_dur_df %>%
  summarise(
    total = n(),
    hazardous = sum(is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid, na.rm = TRUE),
    percentage = mean(is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid, na.rm = TRUE) * 100 
  )
#Graph for this 
neo_dur_df %>%
  count(is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = 100 * n / sum(n),
    status = if_else(is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid, "Hazardous", "Not hazardous") 
    ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = status, y = percentage, fill = status)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(percentage, 2), "%")),
            vjust = -0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Hazardous" = "red",
    "Not hazardous" = "steelblue"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Percent of potentially hazardous aestoriods",
    x = "Classification",
    y = " percentage" ) +
  ylim(0, 100) +
  theme_minimal() 
  
#Consider how this relates to orbit type - 
#APO — Apollo Earth-crossing asteroids whose semi-major axes are larger than Earth's. Their orbits extend farther from the Sun on average, but can cross Earth's orbital path.
#ATE — Aten Earth-crossing asteroids whose semi-major axes are smaller than Earth's. They orbit closer to the Sun on average and have orbital periods shorter than one year.
#AMO — Amor Asteroids that approach Earth's orbit from the outside but do not cross it. Their closest distance to the Sun is slightly beyond Earth's farthest distance from the Sun.
#IEO — Interior Earth Object (Atira) Asteroids with orbits entirely inside Earth's orbital path. Their maximum distance from the Sun is smaller than Earth's minimum distance from the Sun.

orbit_summary <- neo_dur_df %>%
  group_by(orbit_class_type) %>%
  summarise (
    total =n(),
    hazardous = sum(is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid),
    percentage = 100*hazardous / total
  ) 
  
ggplot(orbit_summary,
       aes(x=orbit_class_type, y=percentage, fill = orbit_class_type))+
  geom_col()+
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%")), vjust = -0.5)+
  scale_fill_manual(values =c(
    "AMO" = "steelblue",
    "APO" = "red",
    "ATE" = "orange",
    "IEO" = "purple"
  ))+
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Alfie's Workspace
```{r}
#Making a new data set purely for orbiting body, velocity and miss distance
individual_observations <- neo_dur_df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^(relative_velocity|orbiting_body|miss_distance_kilometers)[0-3]$"),
    names_to = c(".value", "observation"),
    names_pattern = "(relative_velocity|orbiting_body|miss_distance_kilometers)([0-3])"
  )
  

```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
asteroids_analysis <- neo_dur_df %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    changed_planet = n_distinct(c(
      orbiting_body0,
      orbiting_body1,
      orbiting_body2,
      orbiting_body3
    )) > 1
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(asteroids_analysis,
       aes(x = changed_planet, fill = is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    title = "Hazardous Asteroids and Changes in Orbital Planet",
    x = "Did the asteroid change its orbital planet?",
    y = "Proportion of asteroids",
    fill = "Hazardous"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#Displaying a density graph of relative velocities of NEOs 

ggplot(
  data = individual_observations,
  mapping = aes(
    x = relative_velocity,
    colour = is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid)
  ) +
  geom_density() +
  labs(
    x = "Relative Velocity",
    y = "Density",
    colour = "Potentially Hazardous"
  )
```
```{r}
#Displaying a density graph of miss distances for NEOs

ggplot(
  data = individual_observations,
  mapping = aes(
    x = miss_distance_kilometers,
    colour = is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid
  )
) +
  geom_density() +
  labs(
    x = "Miss Distance (Km)",
    y = "Density",
    colour = "Potentially Hazardous"
  )
  
```



Jonah's Workspace
```{r}
# Classifying NEOs based on how close they got to Earth and then comparing this to whether they were deemed hazardous. Less than ~7.5M km is considered a close miss.
neo_dur_df %>%
  filter(orbiting_body0 == "Earth") %>%
  mutate(
    is_close_miss = case_when(
      miss_distance_kilometers0 < 7479894 ~TRUE,
      miss_distance_kilometers0 >= 7479894 ~FALSE
    )) %>% 
  count(is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid, is_close_miss) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_tile(aes(is_close_miss, is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid, fill = n)) +
  labs(
    subtitle = "Objects which missed Earth by less than 7 479 894 km are considered 'close misses'",
    x = "close miss (true / false)",
    y = "hazardous (true / false"
      )

# Investigating the relationship between miss distance, relative velocity and hazard assessment.
neo_dur_df %>%
  filter(orbiting_body0 == "Earth") %>%
  ggplot(aes(miss_distance_kilometers0, relative_velocity0, color = is_potentially_hazardous_asteroid)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    subtitle = "Comparison of Miss Distance and Relative Velocity (first observation) of objects approaching Earth",
    x = "first measured miss distance (km)",
    y = "first measured relative velocity (km)",
    color = "hazardous"
  )
```
